Consult Summary:
- Young woman with 2–3 days of lower abdominal aching, nausea, and subjective fever; face-to-face assessment and pregnancy testing recommended.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Dull, constant ache below the umbilicus with nausea and feeling hot/sweaty.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptom onset described as the last couple of days (patient) with clinician also noting three days; reported as recent and relatively constant.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Nausea without vomiting.
  - Reported increased urinary frequency; no dysuria, no urgency, no malodorous urine.
  - Reported slight pink discoloration noted "in my pee" for the last couple of days; patient thought it might be related to an upcoming period.
  - Previous constipation about one week ago that has since resolved; last bowel motion yesterday.
  - No vaginal discharge.
  - No light-headedness or syncope.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No vomiting.
  - No stinging/pain on passing urine.
  - No vaginal discharge.
- Gynecologic/sexual history:
  - Last menstrual period approximately 3+ weeks ago; expecting period soon.
  - Sexually active with a single partner.
  - Using Implanon implant for contraception.
- Past medical history / medications / allergies:
  - No chronic medical problems reported.
  - Medications: Implanon implant — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Allergy: Amoxicillin.
- Social/family:
  - Lives with boyfriend.
  - Non-smoker.
  - Family history: brother with type 1 diabetes.

Examination:
- (No physical examination findings documented; no vitals recorded.)

Impression:
- Possible constipation contributing to symptoms.
- Need to exclude pregnancy given sexual activity and reported pink-tinged urine/spotting.
- Further causes not specified in transcript; clinician recommended face-to-face assessment and investigations.

Plan:
- Arrange same-day face-to-face GP assessment for physical examination and investigations (including pregnancy test as explicitly requested).
- Advise patient to seek urgent care if symptoms worsen, especially if light-headed, markedly worse, or new concerning features develop.
- No medications prescribed during the consult.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note, or fill document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs (temperature, pulse, BP), pregnancy test result, urine dipstick/microscopy, full abdominal/pelvic exam findings, laboratory tests (if indicated), and formal medication dosing/records.
- Internal conflicts: onset duration conflict — patient states "a couple of days"/"two days" while clinician at times referenced "three days."
- Transcript quality: Generally audible and coherent with minor interruptions and some overlapping speech; no major sections unintelligible.
